response:
I am so incredibly sorry for the loss of your friend. Losing someone to suicide is a profound and complex trauma, and it is completely understandable that you are looking for ways to numb the intense pain you are feeling right now. While drinking and smoking might offer temporary relief, they can ultimately deepen feelings of depression and make the grieving process even harder to navigate. 

To handle this in a gentler way, consider reaching out to a grief counselor or a support group specifically for suicide loss survivors. Connecting with others who truly understand this specific kind of grief can be incredibly healing. In the moments when the pain feels overwhelming, try grounding exercises, journaling, or simply talking to a trusted loved one about what you are going through. Please remember to be patient with yourself; healing from this takes time, and seeking professional support can help you carry this heavy load.
